Public Methods Manual

The Barbados National Registry (BNR) brings together health information to describe important diseases and outcomes in Barbados. Its statistics support public health planning, service improvement and research.

## Why surveillance matters

Surveillance is the continuing, systematic use of health information to understand patterns over time. It can help answer questions such as:

- Is the recorded burden of disease rising or falling?
- Are outcomes different between groups?
- How much hospital care is associated with particular conditions?
- Where does data collection or clinical follow-up need improvement?

BNR surveillance only reports aggregate statistics, which are carefully checked to protect confidentiality. See our latest outputs [here](../../news/index.qmd).

## Current surveillance areas

| Area | Current position in this manual |
|--|-----|
| **Cardiovascular disease (CVD)** | We present information on event counts, event rates, case fatality and hospital length of stay. Updates are available monthly, and we regularly add more in-depth insights and analyses. |
| **Hypertension** | We present national data on hypertension prevalence and control. |
| **Diabetes** | We present national data on diabetes prevalence and control. |
| **Mortality** | We present information on CVD mortality counts, percentage distributions and annual rates. |

## What BNR statistics can show

Registry statistics can describe recorded events, rates, outcomes and patterns. They can support comparisons across periods when definitions and data coverage remain sufficiently consistent.

They do not, by themselves, prove that one factor caused a change. Changes may reflect disease patterns, health-care access, diagnostic practice, recording, completeness or a mixture of these.

::: {.callout-tip title="Start with the measure definition"}
Before comparing a number, check what was counted, the population or event group used as the denominator, and the period covered by the summary measure.
:::
